parsed.canonical_question: Why is the inner mitochondrial membrane important for ATP production?

rendering.title: Inner mitochondrial membrane role
rendering.answer: The inner mitochondrial membrane is critical for ATP production because it is impermeable to protons (hydrogen ions). The electron transport chain pumps protons from the mitochondrial matrix into the intermembrane space, building up a steep electrochemical gradient. Because the inner membrane does not let protons leak back freely, the only route for protons to return to the matrix is through ATP synthase. As protons flow through ATP synthase down their gradient, the enzyme uses that energy to join ADP and phosphate together, producing ATP. If the membrane were leaky, protons would bypass ATP synthase, the gradient would collapse, and ATP synthesis would stop.
